title: Introduce circuitized batch allocator and eviction-safe KV tiers
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: We will replace the existing monolithic batch allocator with a circuitized allocator that exposes per-lane circuit breakers and preemption hooks, and introduce a multi-tier KV cache with an eviction-safe snapshot protocol. Goals are to reduce 95th/99th token latency tail by 12–18% under mixed workloads, lower token cost by enabling safer longer-lived prefixes in the hot tier, and unblock several scheduler backpressure issues.
work_items: Design and validate circuit model for batch lanes: define health signals (queue depth, slot latency, hit-rate) and backpressure thresholds
Implement lightweight lane circuits: per-lane token budget, soft-preempt + graceful draining, and fast-fail path for overloaded lanes
Introduce KV tiers: hot (in-memory, low eviction), warm (compressed/quantized, quick rehydrate), cold (mmapped snapshot) with explicit promotion/demotion APIs
Snapshot-safe eviction protocol: epoched snapshots + lease-less tombstones to avoid losing in-flight KV view during compaction
Scheduler integration: allow circuitized allocator to inform ingress router about lane capacity and preferred prefetch window sizes
Bench harness: create mixed QPS/seqLen traces and SLO runs (100k sample windows) to validate improvements
Migration plan and rollout: feature flag gating, canary at 10% traffic, telemetry dashboards and automatic rollback criteria
progress_notes: 2026-02-20: Architecture review completed with runtime, scheduler, and kv teams. Decided on per-lane circuits rather than global token buckets to reduce head-of-line blocking.
2026-02-26: Prototype circuit gates in the integration branch. Early microbench shows ~9% improvement in median latency under synthetic burst tests.
2026-03-03: KV tier design approved; warm tier will use 4-bit quantized store with fast decode path. Team flagged dependency on new jemalloc upgrade for predictable fragmentation (see ENG-71488).
2026-03-09: Implemented epoched snapshot format and a compact tombstone log. Integration tests for snapshot roundtrip pass on CI with slow-mmap environment.
2026-03-12: Scheduler hooks merged to staging. Observed reduction in backpressure cycles in local cluster by ~22%. Still seeing occasional 95th spike tied to prefetch thrash on zipf workloads.
2026-03-15: Working on preemptive draining logic to avoid evict-then-prefetch storms. Diego to own remaining work on rollout gating and dashboards.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: New eviction protocol may increase cold-start CPU during heavy rehydrate. Mitigation: rate-limit background rehydrates and add per-shard parking to spread work.

Risk: Circuitized preemption could cause higher aborts for latency-sensitive customers. Mitigation: expose knobs per-tenant and default conservative thresholds for Hosted tier; Dedicated tenants can opt-in.
Risk: Dependency upgrades (jemalloc/libaio) may change allocator behavior. Mitigation: isolate in canary clusters and run extended mem/stability tests before release.
metrics_targets: Hot-tier hit rate: +8 percentage points for chat-style workloads
Unit token cost: -10% at 95th percentile workload due to fewer rehydrates and smarter batching
qa_and_validation: Create a replayable mixed-workload trace (customer-shaped) and run A/B against current runtime for 48h
Add synthetic adversarial trace (zipf skew + bursts) to catch thrash scenarios
Memory/FD leak sweeps on CI with stress harness (100x typical concurrency)
rollout_plan: Canary 2: 10% of traffic in staging region with monitoring thresholds
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% by week, with automated rollback on SLO breach
Post-merge: 2-week observation window and postmortem if regressions found
